summary: A 1934 20-foot L-4 lookout in the Clearwater National Forest, abandoned in the 1940s and burned in the 1960s.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1940s and recorded as gone; the Forest Service list gives a 1960s burn.

events.note: 20-foot L-4 tower about half a mile south of the summit
Abandoned in the 1940s; the exact year is not given
Burned in the 1960s; the exact year is not given (Forest Service list only)

evidence.supports: built 1934 as a 20-foot L-4 tower about half a mile south of the summit; abandoned 1940s; gone
evidence.quote: 1934: 20' L-4 tower 1/2 mile south of summit. Abandoned 1940s. Gone.

evidence.supports: Forest Service list calls the structure an L-4 cabin (type column reads cabin)
Forest Service list gives the structure as a 20-foot L-4
Forest Service list gives the distance as 21 miles
Forest Service list measures from Kooskia (ENE of Kooskia)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com calls it a 20-foot L-4 tower; the Forest Service list calls it an L-4 cabin. Both give 1934 and an L-4 structure, so they most likely describe the same lookout.

sources.title: Clearwater National Forest Lookouts (list compiled June 2016)

notes_for_editor: The Forest Service list's header says it draws on Ray Kresek's book, Forest Service records, and Rex Kamstra's firelookout.com site, so it is not fully independent of the two web pages. The 1960s burn appears only in the Forest Service list. The abandonment year is given only as the 1940s; the event year 1940 is a placeholder with the note saying so. The record's kind 'tower' matches firelookout.com; the Forest Service list calls the structure a cabin. The record's status 'gone' matches every source. No photo or site description was found. Firelookout.com and the Forest Service list both give Kooskia as the reference point for the 21-mile distance, so there is no location conflict; the record's coordinates were not checked against Kooskia.
